newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners voting rights in Japan NTV reach 18.48%.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners voting rights in Japan NTV reach 18.48%.

text.p: Nippon Television Network Corp said on Thursday that foreign shareholders held 18.48 percent of its total voting rights as of September 30.

Japanese law stipulates that a private broadcasting company has to lose its broadcasting licence if shares held by foreign individuals, firms, government surpass 20 percent of the company's total voting rights, the company said in a statement.

A broadcasting company is obliged to report the ratio every six months if it reaches 15 percent. An official at Nippon Television, a nationwide broadcaster, said the ratio had been hovering above the 15 percent level for three years.
